cover_lines: Q3 sales climb as unsold stock builds
Blue Line, Pink Line and suburban rail
cover.headline: Bengaluru Builds Out: Rail, Roads and Townships
cover.subhead: Sales are recovering, launches are heavy and infrastructure timelines keep shifting. What it means for buyers across the city and its fast-growing edges.

editor_note.text: The latest quarter brought a firmer market. According to ANAROCK, Bengaluru housing sales rose 12% YoY to 16,670 units in Q3 2026. The agency also says MMR and Bengaluru together accounted for 48% of total sales across the seven cities it tracks, a reminder of how much national demand now rests on these two markets.

Jobs continue to underpin that demand. Colliers says Bengaluru led Jan-Sep 2026 office leasing at 15.7 million sq ft, driven partly by GCCs and flex operators. ANAROCK adds that GCCs made up 70% of the roughly 10.8 million sq ft of office absorption in H1 2026. Where offices cluster, housing follows.

Infrastructure is the other half of the story, and timelines deserve a careful read. BMRCL's Blue Line has reached 72% overall construction progress, per Business Today, yet Construction World reports the full opening has slipped to March 2028. K-RIDE says it is committed to starting suburban rail operations by December 2028. Buy for today's connectivity, not tomorrow's.

insights.subject: STRR Hoskote–Hosur stretch
insights.title: NHAI is looking at opening the 21-km Hoskote–Hosur stretch of the STRR in phases by December with diversions around the unfinished railway overbridge at Lingadeeramallasandra; full ROB completion is expected by March 2027 (Oneindia, 23 Oct).

insights.subject: STRR Hoskote–Hosur stretch
insights.title: Urban Acres on 22 October reported the Hoskote–Karnataka/Tamil Nadu border STRR stretch may open partially by December, depending on an RDSO re-inspection and clearance for a 59-metre girder; the launches are over 1.5 years behind schedule.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Blue Line KR Puram–Marathahalli trial
insights.title: Deccan Herald on 22 October reported Minister Krishna Byre Gowda saying a Blue Line trial run between KR Puram and Marathahalli is expected by October-end (headline only; full article could not be opened). Conflicts with BMRCL MD's 19 Oct statement targeting 15 November.

insights.subject: Namma Metro Pink Line elevated section (Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere)
insights.title: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on about 22 October that the state is awaiting Union government approval to open the 7.5-km Pink Line elevated stretch (Kalena Agrahara–Tavarekere), with operating permission expected in four to five days. No opening date has been confirmed.

insights.subject: ORR Metro barricades / traffic congestion
insights.title: Minister Krishna Byre Gowda on 22 October ordered officials to remove Metro barricades on the Outer Ring Road where construction is complete, saying barricades retained without need were worsening congestion.

insights.subject: Bengaluru Suburban Rail (K-RIDE)
insights.title: The Bengaluru Live reported the 148-km suburban rail network targets April 2030 completion at about ₹23,000 crore, as stated alongside the minister's metro review on 22 October.

insights.subject: STRR Hoskote–Tamil Nadu border (Hosur) 21-km stretch
insights.title: NHAI is exploring opening the 21-km Hoskote–Hosur STRR stretch in phases as early as December, but the railway overbridge at Lingadeeramallasandra may not be complete until March 2027, with a 59-m girder launch awaiting clearances; the bottleneck has persisted over 18 months.

insights.subject: Hebbal Short Tunnel tree felling
insights.title: The Greater Bengaluru Authority received more than 1,500 objections to the proposed felling of 1,128 trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel project, The News Minute reported on 21 October 2026.

insights.subject: Hebbal Short Tunnel NGT interim order
insights.title: The National Green Tribunal has restrained the Bangalore Development Authority from felling any trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel until the next hearing on 15 December, per The News Minute (21 Oct 2026).

insights.subject: Hebbal Short Tunnel tree-felling objections
insights.title: Greater Bengaluru Authority received more than 1,500 objections to the proposed felling of 1,128 trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel project; objections will go to the tree expert committee and the BDA, which is implementing the project (TNM, 21 Oct).
